A `svelte-ignore` comment silences a warning of the Svelte compiler. Once the code it was written for has changed, the comment silences nothing, but it still reads as if something was wrong there, and it would hide a new warning of that kind. Each code in such a comment that the compiler doesn't warn about is reported, and so is a comment without any code.

The warnings come from the `svelte/compiler` that the project has installed, as eslint-plugin-svelte gets them: the scripts are compiled after TypeScript has transformed them, and a style sheet with a `lang` is transformed with the preprocessor the project has for it, `sass`, `less`, `stylus` or PostCSS. A style sheet that no installed preprocessor reads is left out, and comments about its selectors count as used. A comment applies to the element or the block after it, and to everything in it. A component that the compiler can't compile gets no reports about codes.

Compiling a component runs the project's JavaScript: `svelte/compiler` of the `eslint-plugin-svelte` that the config loads, the preprocessors, and the PostCSS and Babel config files of the working directory. So the rule only reports where an ESLint config file loads `eslint-plugin-svelte`. Turned on any other way, as from `bunfig.toml` or `--rule`, it reports nothing.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-unused-svelte-ignore": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<!-- svelte-ignore a11y_missing_attribute -->
<img src="/logo.png" alt="Acme" />

<!-- svelte-ignore -->
<p>Saved</p>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<!-- svelte-ignore a11y_missing_attribute -->
<div>
  {#if user}
    <img src={user.avatar} />
  {/if}
</div>
```
